target_customer: Hospitals and health systems that hold surplus or pre-owned medical equipment and supplies
problem: Hospitals lack visibility into their equipment inventory and have no easy way to resell or redeploy surplus assets, so they waste money and stock.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on used medical equipment plus asset management software
product_category: Healthcare asset management and used equipment marketplace

founders.name: Chloe Alpert
founders.background_notes: YC page lists her as Founder/CEO, now an investor. The 2019 NFX seed press release calls her co-founder and CEO. A third-party profile says she won a $500,000 competition in October 2017 (single source, not used as fact).

founders.name: Tim Growney
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC company page as founder and CTO; no bio there.

exit.reason: A website notice announcing it was ceasing operations was seen by January 2022 per a third-party profile; the company gave no public reason found.

competitors.name: Cohealo
competitors.what: Software and logistics letting hospitals share and mobilize medical equipment between facilities
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the cited source
competitors.funding_then: $9M Series A in 2014 (Romulus Capital, Krillion Ventures)

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided marketplace plus inventory tracking software is standard web engineering; the hard parts were logistics and hospital data integration.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on liquidity of buyers and sellers, but no exclusive data or contracts are documented and equipment resale brokers already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it; the company ended operations by early 2022.

market_need_then: Hospitals hold large pools of idle equipment; the 2018 and 2019 press describe the aim of recovering money from surplus assets, but no spend figures were found.

branding.domain_note: Used medinas.com; a third-party profile says the domain later hosted a liquidation firm.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered funding, but no coverage of the brand itself was found.

outcome_analysis: Medinas raised a $1M seed in 2018 and a $5M seed led by NFX in October 2019, then reportedly posted a closure notice by January 2022. The company has not published why it ended. The factor listed is an inference from the absence of any later round after the 2019 seed and the timing during the pandemic hospital spending shock, so treat the cause as not public.
notes: YC record lists no website; medinas.com later reportedly hosts an unrelated firm, so the site is treated as dead. Totals conflict: CB Insights says $7.37M over six rounds including a $0.25M PPP loan (undated, not recorded as a round), SeedTable says $8M, Parsers $6M. The 2018 seed rests on one outlet plus aggregators. The WeWork award is stated in the 2019 press release. The closure date and cause come from a single third-party profile. Education and prior employers for Alpert and Growney not found in opened sources. Other CB Insights named rivals (OpenMarkets, BidMed) lack sources dated near the batch.
